items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: We had Bill Moore on the bass

ctx.x: That's right. And we had Carl George on trumpet. Carl George used to play with Stan Kenton. He's a black boy that went to school and studied under Gustave. And he played one of the most beautiful trumpets you ever

heard in your life. He played first trumpet in Stan Kenton's band for about five years, didn't he? About five years. Earl George. He played with us. We had Torran on the trombone. We had Bill Moore on the bass, Chester Lane on the piano. That was when Count Basie started giving us some arrangements, you know, and we used to rehearse arrangements. And we brought in Larry Steele to produce the shows. He came in.

And we had this boy, Bob Parrish from California, who sang -- I forget the song -- "Donkey Serenade." And of course we had Ted Smith for vocalist. The band still drew big crowds, and we made friends and Sleepy Tomlin was working with the band.
